correctness.rationale: The known exact subtree enumeration gives R1,R2. A uniform balanced log expansion has a first-order coefficient 3k/2-(i-j)^2 whose binomial average is k/2, matching the prelimit parameter; a second-order computation yields 7/(2e^2). A proportional unbalanced expansion gives a strictly negative squared first-order residual. Leaf-extension double counting bounds all coefficient tails factorially, while a local three-probability witness proves matching TV lower bounds. Checker replay: 310 finite and asymptotic comparisons, not used as infinite proof.
